title: Set Matrix Zeroes
statement: You get a grid of integers. Wherever a cell is 0, turn its entire row and its entire column into 0. Do the change inside the same grid. The best answers use only a constant amount of extra memory.

example.caption: One zero in the middle wipes the whole middle row and the whole middle column.

idea.sentence: Use row 0 and column 0 as free notepads that say which rows and columns to wipe, and keep two flags for whether row 0 and column 0 held a real zero themselves.

jargon.plain: A 0 written into the first cell of a row (column 0) or the first cell of a column (row 0) to say: wipe this row, or wipe this column.
Only a fixed handful of variables beyond the grid, no matter how big the grid is.

watch.inputHint: One argument: a matrix of integers (equal-length rows), like [[1,0],[3,4]].

vars.meaning: number of columns, so the grid has m times n cells

compare.bruteLabel: Two lists of rows and columns to wipe

rows.name: Copy of the grid
rows.note: Zero into a copy while reading the original. Simple, but it doubles the memory.

rows.name: Row and column lists
rows.note: Remember which rows and columns hold a zero in two small arrays, then wipe.

rows.name: Markers in row 0 and column 0
rows.note: The first row and column act as those two lists. Two boolean flags protect their own zeros.

fast.takeaway: Every cell must be read at least once, so mn is the floor. The three answers differ only in where the notes are kept: a copy, two lists, or the grid itself.

stages.title: Flag row 0 and column 0
stages.note: Before they turn into marker space, remember whether each already holds a real zero.

stages.title: Mark
stages.note: Scan the inside cells. A zero at (r, c) writes 0 at (r, 0) and (0, c).

stages.title: Wipe the inside
stages.note: Scan the inside cells again. If its row marker or column marker is 0, the cell becomes 0.

stages.title: Wipe row 0 and column 0
stages.note: Last of all, use the two flags to zero row 0 and column 0 if they had a real zero.

edges.title: Real zero in row 0 only
edges.why: Row 0 is wiped, but rows 1 and 2 are not. A zero in row 0 is a column marker, never a row marker.

edges.title: Real zero in column 0 only
edges.why: Row 1 and column 0 get wiped. Without a column flag, a zero in column 0 looks like a marker for a zero that is not there.

edges.title: One cell, a zero
edges.why: There are no inside cells. Both flags are true and wiping row 0 and column 0 changes nothing.

edges.title: Single row
edges.why: There are no inside rows. The row flag alone carries the whole answer.

gotchas.text: Compute both flags before you write any marker. Marking first overwrites row 0 and column 0, so you can no longer tell a real zero from a marker.
Wipe the inside cells before row 0 and column 0. The markers must still be intact while the inside is being read. Zeroing row 0 first erases every column marker.
Scan the inside cells only (from index 1). If the mark pass also visited row 0 and column 0, it would read its own markers as new zeros and wipe too much.
To keep the original grid, copy it with matrix.map((row) => [...row]). Both matrix.slice() and [...matrix] copy only the outer array, so the rows are shared and the 'copy' gets zeroed too.

The function takes a [][]int and edits the shared rows, so the caller sees the change with no return value. A test that wants the original must copy every row first, because copying the outer slice shares the rows.

recap.key: Store the wipe-this-row and wipe-this-column notes in row 0 and column 0, guarded by two flags, and apply them in the right order.
recap.complexity: Time O(m x n). Space O(1).
moves: Flags: does row 0 or column 0 hold a real zero?
Inside cells: a zero marks (r, 0) and (0, c)
Inside cells again: marker says wipe
Last: wipe row 0 and column 0 using the flags
